what: Behind the dark panel, a faint (.14) 1.25px dot sits at every corner of a 56px cell grid (one WebGL2 shader, with the outer 12% at the edges faded). When the mouse is over the panel, dots within 150px brighten by .6 (Gaussian light), and cells inside the radius light up by distance (dot max .9 · cell fill .06), hold for .4s, then fade out over .8s, leaving a trail where the cursor has passed. The mouse position follows with a .07s time constant. Pressing sends out a ripple ring from that spot at 600px per second (weaker with distance) that sweeps across the cells. Because it uses difference blending, the dots look black over the giant white text placed on top

options.hold: Time to hold a lit cell (ms), default 400
options.spot: Light intensity around the mouse, default .6
options.edge: Edge blur share, default .12 — 0 keeps it sharp to the edge

use: <footer data-fx="dot-grid-spot" style="background: var(--kf-contrast-bg); color: var(--kf-contrast-ink)">… Text is position: relative; z-index: 2 …</footer>
note: Dot color is --kf-contrast-ink (falls back to text color). The original also has an ambient option that lights random cells on their own, but it is off, so it was left out. The delay used when the panel comes within 2.5 screens of the document end is left to the consumer
